direction: Test a capacity tie-break with a strict shortlist boundary.
hypothesis: A strict tie boundary may retain useful packing decisions while preventing overly large correction terms from promoting unrelated choices.

operations.mechanism: Keep the linear base score and depot rule. Build the same near-tie mask, rank only its members by a bounded capacity-fit secondary score, and return no candidate outside the mask when the tie branch triggers.

preserve: Keep the existing CVRP interface, read-only inputs, feasibility and deterministic evaluation. Preserve useful incumbent structure unless the mechanism calls for a deliberate pivot.
reasoning_summary: Candidate 1 improved to 10.91967. It retained the 0.60 radial term, added a residual-capacity penalty divided by current distance when near ties existed, and then compared every candidate. A node outside the mask can therefore win. The main gain is on instance 2; instances 4 and 5 regressed. Use the selected complete in-run Memory record as advisory context.
